title: Pap test (cervical smear)
what: The gynecologist takes cells from your cervix with a soft brush. They are checked under a microscope to find early changes that could turn into cancer.
why: For regular cervical cancer screening, and if past tests showed changes. Often done together with an HPV test.
duration: the test itself takes 1 to 2 minutes, and results usually take 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: The first day of your last period
If past smears showed changes, or you had treatment on your cervix
If you have had the HPV vaccine

prepare.title: Your cycle
prepare.text: Not during your period. The middle of your cycle is usually best. Check with your doctor.

prepare.title: 2 days before
prepare.text: No sex, douching, suppositories, creams, or vaginal tablets.

prepare.title: Exams
prepare.text: If you recently had an exam with gel or a colposcopy, tell your doctor. The smear is sometimes moved to another day.

steps: You undress below the waist and lie on the exam chair
The doctor gently inserts a disposable speculum
A soft brush collects cells from your cervix. It takes a few seconds
The sample goes into a small jar with liquid or onto a glass slide
feel: A brief pulling feeling when the cells are taken
after: Light spotting during the day is normal
If the result shows changes, the doctor will order a repeat test or an exam. This does not mean you have cancer
Your doctor will tell you how often to repeat it, based on the screening program
red_flags: Strong pain or heavy bleeding after the test: see a doctor or call emergency services

faq.q: How often do I need a Pap test?
faq.a: Usually every 3 to 5 years, depending on your age and your HPV test results. Your doctor will tell you your schedule.

faq.q: Does an abnormal Pap test mean cancer?
faq.a: Usually not. More often it is cell changes that are easy to treat. That is what screening is for.
Usually not. It is unpleasant, but quick. Relax and breathe calmly.

reminders.text: Pap test in 2 days. Starting today, no sex, douching, suppositories, or creams.
